_about: Rotation seeds for the daily non-place X posts. Facts here are already on hcmcinsider.com; posts must not add new facts.

tips.facts: Tap a contactless Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Amex or UnionPay card, Apple Pay or Samsung Pay at the gate; tap out with the same card. Single trip 7,000–20,000 dong; 1-day pass 40,000; 3-day pass 90,000.
Mon–Fri 5am–10pm, weekends and holidays until 11pm. Trains every 6–8 min at rush hour, 10–12 min otherwise. Ben Thanh to Suoi Tien in about 30 min.

tips.topic: City buses are free until 31 Dec 2026
tips.facts: 134 city bus routes are free until 31 Dec 2026. Since 1 Oct, tap a contactless card or phone when boarding to record the trip; nothing is charged.

tips.topic: Airport to the city by bus
tips.facts: Bus 152 runs from Tan Son Nhat airport via Ben Thanh Market; bus 109 goes to Saigon bus station near Ben Thanh. Both are on the city's free-fare list until 31 Dec 2026.
From Bach Dang pier in District 1 towards Linh Dong, about 15,000 dong a trip, first boats from 8:30am. Great skyline views.

tips.topic: Cu Chi Tunnels by public bus
tips.facts: Bus 13 from Saigon bus station to Cu Chi bus station, then bus 79 to Ben Duoc. Allow 2+ hours each way; most visitors take a tour.
Walk at a slow, steady pace and don't stop suddenly. Riders steer around you. Raise a hand to be seen.
Small stalls take cash in dong; many shops accept bank-app QR. Keep small notes: 10,000–50,000 dong covers most street dishes.
Phone and bag snatching from passing motorbikes happens. Keep your phone away from the street side and bags zipped and across your body.
Cover shoulders and knees, take off your hat, speak softly, and ask before photographing people praying.
Choose busy stalls where food is cooked in front of you. Drink bottled water. Start with cooked dishes like noodle soups.
113 police, 114 fire, 115 ambulance, free from any phone in Vietnam. Ask your hotel or a shop owner to call if you don't speak Vietnamese.
May to November usually brings short, heavy afternoon showers rather than all-day rain. Carry a light rain jacket.
Look for 'chay' (vegetarian). Chay shops are busiest on the 1st and 15th days of the lunar month; some only open on those days.

tips.topic: Get an eSIM before you land
tips.facts: Install an eSIM at home and switch it on after landing so ride-hailing and maps work right away.
Checked out at noon but flying at night? Leave luggage at a storage spot and spend the afternoon eating instead of dragging a suitcase.

tips.topic: Saigon or Ho Chi Minh City?
tips.facts: The official name is Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC). Many locals still say Saigon, especially for the old centre; you'll see both on signs and maps.
Cholon is Ho Chi Minh City's historic Chinatown, around the old Districts 5, 6 and 11: noodle shops, dim sum, herbal duck noodles, sweet soups, old markets and Chinese assembly halls.
Tipping isn't expected at local eateries; it's appreciated at spas, on tours and in upscale restaurants.
